notes.headline: Nothing needs fixing — this bounce is clean and ready to hand off for mastering.
notes.summary: MixCheck found no technical problems in this 0:40 stereo mix, and it scores 10.0/10. True peak sits at -2.16 dBTP with 8.6 dB of peak-to-loudness, so there's room for a mastering engineer to work. Stereo behaviour is solid too: L/R correlation 0.78, mono loss only 0.51 dB, and the left/right balance is within -0.04 dB. Since this is going to mastering, don't chase the -10.72 LUFS integrated number — loudness is the mastering stage's job.
listen_for: Check the mix in mono once more to confirm nothing hollows out — the measured mono loss of 0.51 dB says it should hold up.
Listen on a small speaker or phone to confirm the low end translates; low-end correlation of 0.78 suggests it will.
Spot-check the loudest section for anything that feels pinched, even though true peak is -2.16 dBTP.
strengths: True peak of -2.16 dBTP with 8.6 dB peak-to-loudness leaves real headroom for mastering.
Stereo image is well behaved: 0.78 L/R correlation and only 0.51 dB mono loss.
Left/right balance is essentially centred at -0.04 dB.
